meanings.note: Contrast. Core Russian conj meaning 'and, but; so' in everyday speech.
Starting a question: а жвачку?. Core Russian conj meaning 'and, but; so' in everyday speech.

examples.trans: And this is for you.
And where's the toy car?
Dad, did you bring any gum?

meanings.note: Common masculine noun meaning 'bar, pub' in everyday Russian.

examples.trans: Our bar is closing.

examples.text: Проверьте все бары и старых друзей.
examples.trans: Check all the bars and old friends.
It is already morning. Our bar is closing.

meanings.note: Declinable masculine noun meaning 'bartender', changing its case ending across all six Russian grammatical cases to mark its role in the clause.

examples.trans: The bartender poured the wine.

examples.text: Бармен, принесите нам бокал белого вина!
examples.trans: Bartender, bring us a glass of white wine!

examples.text: Бармен наливает холодную воду в стакан.
examples.trans: The bartender pours cold water into the glass.

meanings.en: to run (in one direction), to flee, to escape
meanings.note: irregular mixed conjugation: бегу, бежишь, ..., бегут

examples.trans: Run, Marina, before it's too late!
Where are you running so fast?

examples.text: Надо бежать! Беги в деревню к маме.
examples.trans: You need to run! Run to the village to your mum's.

meanings.note: Common feminine noun meaning 'slip of paper, document' in everyday Russian.

examples.trans: He wrote the number on a slip of paper.
This piece of paper has no legal power.

examples.text: Такую бумажку можно купить в любом переходе.
examples.trans: You can buy such a paper in any underpass.

meanings.note: the comparative 'быстрее', often as an order
the comparative 'быстрее', often as an order

examples.trans: Faster!
He drives fast.

examples.text: Виталик, почему мы так медленно едем? Быстрее!
examples.trans: Vitalik, why are we going so slowly? Faster!

meanings.note: + prepositional (where). Core Russian prep meaning 'in, into' in everyday speech.
+ accusative (where to). Core Russian prep meaning 'in, into' in everyday speech.

examples.trans: How is it in Hungary?
I grew up in a communal flat.
Hello! How was it in Hungary?

meanings.note: The neuter form 'всё' used alone. Core Russian det meaning 'all, whole; everyone, everything' in everyday speech.
Neuter всё. Core Russian det meaning 'all, whole; everyone, everything' in everyday speech.
Plural все. Core Russian det meaning 'all, whole; everyone, everything' in everyday speech.

examples.trans: Everything's fine.
As you all know...
Share with everyone.

meanings.note: polite to one person, or to several people

meanings.en: other forms: вас (gen/acc), вам (dat), вами (instr), вас (prep)
meanings.note: Case forms. Core Russian pron meaning 'you (polite or plural)' in everyday speech.

examples.trans: As you all know...
Does the governor support you?

examples.text: Спасибо, спасибо! Как вы все знаете, я родился и вырос в Синеозерске.
examples.trans: Thank you, thank you! As you all know, I was born and grew up in Sineozersk.

meanings.note: 'закрывать глаза на' + accusative = to turn a blind eye to

examples.text: Я не буду закрывать на это глаза.
examples.trans: I'm not going to close my eyes to this.
She has blue eyes.

examples.text: А я глаза на это закрывать не буду. Я подниму людей!
examples.trans: Well, I'm not going to close my eyes to this. I'll rally people!

meanings.en: hot (to the touch, of food/drink, not weather)
meanings.note: Agrees in gender, number, and case with the noun it modifies ('hot').

examples.trans: Arkasha, here's some hot tea.
Careful, the cup is very hot.

examples.text: Аркаша, держи горячий чай. И бутерброд с вареньем ешь.
examples.trans: Arkasha, here's some hot tea. And eat a jam sandwich.

meanings.note: emphatic at the start of a sentence
Disbelief. Core Russian part meaning 'yes' in everyday speech.

examples.trans: Oh yeah?
Yes, it's me.
Oh yeah? When?

meanings.note: + genitive. Core Russian prep meaning 'for' in everyday speech.

examples.trans: We could open a salon for you.
This is for you.

examples.text: Для вас можно открыть салон красоты.
examples.trans: We could open a beauty salon for you.

meanings.note: Baking compartment of a stove. Common feminine noun meaning 'oven' in everyday Russian.

examples.trans: Can you believe it, they forgot it in the oven!
The pie is in the oven.

examples.text: Представляешь, в духовке забыли! Юль, выйди.
examples.trans: Can you believe it, they forgot it in the oven! Yul, step out.

meanings.note: condition: если хочешь = if you want; а если нет? = and if not?

examples.trans: Come if you want.
And if not?
Take her if you want.

meanings.note: baked dish of mushrooms, cheese, and cream

examples.trans: Cook a delicious julienne.

examples.text: И фаршируй рыбу жюльеном с лимоном.
examples.trans: And stuff the fish with julienne and lemon.

meanings.note: Prefix 'за-' marks beginning an action, covering, or stopping by along the way (stem 'метить'). Used in Russian as an perfective verb focusing on a single completed action or result meaning 'to notice', forming an aspectual pair with 'замечать'.

examples.trans: He did not notice the loss.

examples.text: Никто на кухне ничего не заметил.
examples.trans: Nobody in the kitchen noticed anything.
And what if someone notices me?

meanings.note: emphasis: вот поэтому ты и... = that's exactly why you...

examples.trans: I was born and grew up here.
Dad and Mum.

examples.text: Спасибо, спасибо! Как вы все знаете, я родился и вырос в Синеозерске.
examples.trans: Thank you, thank you! As you all know, I was born and grew up in Sineozersk.

meanings.note: вот именно = that's just it, quite right
А именно = namely. Core Russian part meaning 'exactly, namely, precisely' in everyday speech.

examples.trans: Exactly, quite right.

examples.text: Именно это я и хотел сказать.
examples.trans: That is justamente what I wanted to say.

examples.text: Вот именно. Но мне сдаваться нельзя.
examples.trans: Exactly. But I must not give up.

meanings.note: + dative. Core Russian prep meaning 'to, towards' in everyday speech.

examples.trans: There's someone here to see you.
I'm going to Mum's.

examples.text: Аркадий Борисович, извините, тут к вам человек.
examples.trans: Arkady Borisovich, I'm sorry, there's a man here to see you.

meanings.note: In questions. Core Russian det meaning 'what; what a' in everyday speech.
in exclamations: какой грязный! = how dirty!

examples.trans: What is your town like?
What a beautiful house!

examples.text: Смотрите, какой у нас грязный унитаз!
examples.trans: Look, how dirty our toilet is!

meanings.note: genitive also 'коньяку' (some cognac)

examples.trans: He drinks French cognac.
The cognac is very expensive.
And you're drinking French cognac yourself.

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian personal or demonstrative pronoun meaning 'someone', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.text: Кто-то не оценил твой отличный ход?
examples.trans: Did someone not appreciate your great move?
Finally someone is for the people!

examples.text: Слушай, тут пишут: «Гордость России! Наконец-то кто-то за народ!»
examples.trans: Listen, here they write: 'Pride of Russia! Finally someone is for the people!'

meanings.note: Declinable masculine noun meaning 'lemon', changing its case ending across all six Russian grammatical cases to mark its role in the clause.

examples.trans: Add a slice of lemon.

examples.text: И фаршируй рыбу жюльеном с лимоном.
examples.trans: And stuff the fish with julienne and lemon.

meanings.note: Adjective formed with the common Slavic suffix '-н-' from a noun/verb root. Agrees in gender, number, and case with the noun it modifies ('meat (attributive)').

examples.trans: Meat dishes are very filling.

examples.text: Но сочные мясные котлеты такие вкусные!
examples.trans: But juicy meat cutlets are so tasty!

examples.text: Скажи, что это для мясного соуса.
examples.trans: Say that this is for meat sauce.

meanings.note: + prepositional: на сайте. Core Russian prep meaning 'on, onto; for' in everyday speech.
+ accusative: на второй срок. Core Russian prep meaning 'on, onto; for' in everyday speech.

examples.trans: The programme is on the website.
He is running for a second term.

examples.text: Я очень люблю наш город. Поэтому я иду на второй срок.
examples.trans: I love our town very much. That's why I'm running for a second term.

meanings.en: name, title (of an object, place, or dish)
meanings.note: Prefix 'на-' marks surface contact, accumulation, or completing a quantity (stem 'звание'). Verbal action/result neuter noun formed with '-ение'/'-ание'. Common neuter noun meaning 'name, title' in everyday Russian.

examples.trans: I wrote the name on a piece of paper.

examples.text: Я написал название на этой бумажке.
examples.trans: I wrote the name on this piece of paper.

examples.text: Ты просто изменил старые названия на новые!
examples.trans: You simply changed old names to new ones!

meanings.note: Prefix 'на-' marks surface contact, accumulation, or completing a quantity (stem 'писать'). Used as an perfective (single completed action) verb meaning 'to write', paired with 'писать'.

examples.trans: He wrote a statement.
Write to me.

examples.text: А зачем? Я сам сделал так, чтобы он его написал.
examples.trans: And why would I? I'm the one who made him write it.

meanings.en: it is necessary, one needs to
meanings.note: + dative of the person + infinitive: мне нужно позвонить

examples.trans: I need to make a call.
You need to rest.

examples.text: Мне нужно позвонить губернатору. Дай телефон.
examples.trans: I need to call the governor. Give me a phone.

meanings.note: short form 'нужен / нужна / нужно / нужны' + dative: 'мне нужна работа' = I need a job

examples.trans: I need a job too.
Do you need a pen?
He needs money.

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian personal or demonstrative pronoun meaning 'to her', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.text: Она нашла нас на новом месте.
examples.trans: She found us at the new place.
That is it, she got really offended.
She is not answering her phone.

meanings.note: chiefly used in the idiom для отвода глаз

examples.trans: This is needed to keep up appearances.

examples.text: В бар сходи для отвода глаз.
examples.trans: Go to the bar to keep up appearances.

meanings.en: to come up to, to approach
meanings.note: К + dative. Prefix 'под-' ('under, up to') indicates approaching or supporting from below (stem 'ойти'). Used as an perfective (single completed action) verb meaning 'to come up (to), to approach', paired with 'подходить'.

Prefix 'под-' ('under, up to') indicates approaching or supporting from below (stem 'ойти'). Used as an perfective (single completed action) verb meaning 'to come up (to), to approach', paired with 'подходить'.

examples.trans: Come here to me!
Keep away from my child!

examples.text: Нам не нужна ваша приставка! Ещё раз подойдёте к моему ребёнку — пожалеете!
examples.trans: We don't need your console! Come near my child again and you'll be sorry!

meanings.note: Informal. Core Russian interj meaning 'bye' in everyday speech.
As an adverb. Core Russian interj meaning 'bye' in everyday speech.

examples.trans: Bye!
Bye, Dad!
Bye, darling!

meanings.note: Понял? = got it?; понял = got it. Prefix 'по-' forms perfective verbs or marks a brief/onset action (stem 'нять'). Used as an perfective (single completed action) verb meaning 'to understand', paired with 'понимать'.

examples.trans: Got it?
I didn't understand.
Share it all equally with everyone, understand?

meanings.note: Core Russian adv meaning 'then, later, afterwards' in everyday speech.

examples.trans: First coffee, then work.
I'll call later.
And then waste will flow.

meanings.note: Prefix 'при-' indicates approaching, attachment, or slight degree of action (stem 'нести'). Used as an perfective (single completed action) verb meaning 'to bring (on foot)', paired with 'приносить'.

examples.text: А я вот вам чаю с сушками принёс.
examples.trans: I've brought you some tea and bread rings.
Bring some water, please.
What did you bring into the flat?

meanings.note: Animal or food. Common feminine noun meaning 'fish' in everyday Russian.

examples.trans: A big platter of fish and crabs.

examples.text: На ужин мы приготовили свежую рыбу.
examples.trans: For dinner we cooked fresh fish.

examples.text: У нас есть большая тарелка рыбы и крабов.
examples.trans: We have a big platter of fish and crabs.

meanings.note: + instrumental; со before some consonant clusters: со всеми

examples.trans: Share with everyone.
I'm with Dad.
Share it all equally with everyone, understand?

meanings.note: Prefix 'с-' ('together' or 'down from') marks convergence or completion (stem 'делать'). Used as an perfective (single completed action) verb meaning 'to do, to make', paired with 'делать'.

examples.trans: We've done a lot.
I'll do it tomorrow.

examples.text: Мы сделали много, но надо сделать ещё больше.
examples.trans: We've done a lot, but we need to do even more.

meanings.note: once; что скажешь? = what do you say?

Polite request. Prefix 'с-' ('together' or 'down from') marks convergence or completion (stem 'казать'). Used as an perfective (single completed action) verb meaning 'to say, to tell', paired with 'говорить'.

examples.trans: What did you say?
Excuse me, where's the metro?
Tell us, when will your programme be out?

meanings.note: + accusative. Prefix 'с-' ('together' or 'down from') marks convergence or completion (stem 'лушать'). Used as an imperfective (ongoing/repeated action) verb meaning 'to listen', paired with 'послушать'.
the imperative 'слушай' starts a sentence, like 'look, ...'

'Слушаю' = I'm listening. Prefix 'с-' ('together' or 'down from') marks convergence or completion (stem 'лушать'). Used as an imperfective (ongoing/repeated action) verb meaning 'to listen', paired with 'послушать'.

examples.trans: Listen, Samson.
Yes, I'm listening.

examples.text: Слушай, Самсон, я тут подумал. Твой начальник — такой опытный специалист.
examples.trans: Listen, Samson, I've been thinking. Your boss is such an experienced specialist.

meanings.note: Prefix 'с-' ('together' or 'down from') marks convergence or completion (stem 'лушаться'). Used in Russian as an imperfective verb expressing ongoing, habitual, or repeated action meaning 'to obey', forming an aspectual pair with 'послушаться'. The reflexive suffix '-ся'/'-сь' makes the action intransitive, reciprocal, or directed at the subject.

examples.trans: Understood, chef!
Understood, chef! I will find the knife.

examples.text: Слушаюсь, шеф, я сделаю всё моментально.
examples.trans: Understood, chef, I will do everything instantly.

meanings.note: culinary condiment or liquid topping

examples.text: Паста под соусом была очень вкусной.
examples.trans: The pasta with sauce was very tasty.
The chef prepared a spicy tomato sauce.

examples.text: Сегодня на ужин паста под соусом!
examples.trans: Tonight for dinner we have pasta with sauce!

meanings.en: to put, to place in an upright position
meanings.note: Takes accusative. Prefix 'с-' ('together' or 'down from') marks convergence or completion (stem 'тавить'). Used as an imperfective (ongoing/repeated action) verb meaning 'to put, to place', paired with 'поставить'.

examples.trans: Where should I put the plate?
Put the kettle on the table.

examples.text: Успокойтесь, я ещё сделаю! Куда ставить тарелку?
examples.trans: Calm down, I'll make more! Where should I put the plate?

meanings.en: to go and come back, to pop over
meanings.note: 'Сходите!' = Go on, go and see. Prefix 'с-' ('together' or 'down from') marks convergence or completion (stem 'ходить'). Used as an perfective (single completed action) verb meaning 'to go (somewhere and come back)', paired with 'ходить'.

examples.trans: Yes, go on.
I'll pop to the shop.
Yes, go on. Don't mix it up with another one!

meanings.note: the comparative 'тише' = quieter, used as 'shh'
тише! (comparative) = quiet! keep it down!

examples.trans: Quiet, the children are asleep!
It's quiet here.
Quiet!

meanings.note: уже четыре года = for four years now

examples.text: Я уже четыре года работаю мэром.
examples.trans: I've been mayor for four years now.
Dad is already home.
I'm already home.

meanings.note: Used as an imperfective (ongoing/repeated action) verb meaning 'to stuff, fill (culinary)'.

examples.trans: Stuff the fish with lemon.

examples.text: И фаршируй рыбу жюльеном с лимоном.
examples.trans: And stuff the fish with julienne and lemon.

meanings.note: Question word. Core Russian pron meaning 'what' in everyday speech.
Conjunction. Core Russian pron meaning 'what' in everyday speech.
Core Russian pron meaning 'what' in everyday speech.

examples.trans: What's this?
Look what I've got.

examples.text: Привет! Смотри, что у меня есть.
examples.trans: Hi! Look what I've got.

meanings.note: pointing at a thing or a situation; 'это' + noun = 'this is ...'
points at something: это моё = that's mine
Linking word: главное — это народ. Core Russian pron meaning 'this, that; it is' in everyday speech.

meanings.en: other forms: этого, этому, это, этим, этом
meanings.note: Case forms. Core Russian pron meaning 'this, that; it is' in everyday speech.

examples.trans: That's mine.
And this is for you.
And this is for you. A toy car!

meanings.note: alone: 'я этого не хочу' = I don't want that

examples.trans: This house.
I'm sick of this communal flat.

examples.text: Меня уже тошнит от этой коммуналки! У нас труба уже неделю течёт.
examples.trans: I'm sick of this communal flat! Our pipe has been leaking for a week now.

meanings.note: меня = me (genitive/accusative), мне = to me (dative)

meanings.en: other forms: меня (gen/acc), мне (dat), мной (instr), мне (prep)
meanings.note: Case forms. Core Russian pron meaning 'I' in everyday speech.

examples.trans: I'm doing my homework.
I grew up here.
Chef, I didn't take it.
